elements.element: Preferred: no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer (Company)
elements.evidence: "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment" remains operative

elements.element: Preferred: no penalty-style termination payment formula
elements.evidence: "aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two" is retained

elements.element: Fallback: amount characterised as an early-termination fee
elements.evidence: "The Termination Payment is an early termination fee"
"capped at three (3) months' fees payable by the Company under Section 3.1 preceding the Termination Date"

elements.element: Fallback: it is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "is the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company under this Agreement"

reasons: Locked target is the fallback, and all three fallback atoms are present in one inserted sentence: early-termination fee characterisation, a 3 months' fees cap, and exclusivity as the sole liquidated amount.
Preferred is not met and was not targeted: the Net Sales-based termination payment obligation survives, so a liquidated amount remains payable by the Company.
Minimality holds: a single concise appended paragraph caps the existing formula rather than rewriting or deleting clauses (a) and (c); no other level's requirements or new exceptions were imported.

Intent preserved: the payment schedule in (c) and the Net Sales computation continue to operate subject to the ceiling, and no undefined term is created (the 3 months' fees are tied to the existing Section 3.1 fee mechanic).

Minor drafting note only, not a deviation: "three (3) months' fees payable ... under Section 3.1 preceding the Termination Date" would read more cleanly as the three months immediately preceding the Termination Date, and the cap's precedence over the clause (a) formula could be stated as "notwithstanding paragraph (a)".
